source_updates.title: A DDSP Framework for Adaptive Room Equalization
findings: the system adapts a playback or room equalizer and is not a creative track equalizer
the target response is derived from the initial measured room impulse response rather than an independent artistic or multi-position target
evaluation uses ten MedleyDB full mixes in a controlled linear simulation driven by measured SoundCam room impulse responses
the 8192-sample frame, 5 percent new estimate and 95 percent history, and optimizer settings are experiment-specific parameters rather than live-sound presets
runtime was measured on an RTX 5090 without audio I/O or operating-system jitter
crowd noise at low SNR, electroacoustic nonlinearities, converter quantization, thermal drift and uncontrolled listener motion were excluded
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Treat the method as evidence for differentiable closed-loop room-calibration research, not as a creative mix-EQ rule or proof of safe deployment on the project's target hardware.

source_updates.title: A Clipping Prevention Method for All-Pass Digital Filters with Time-Varying Coefficients
findings: the method algebraically limits coefficient increments for first- and second-order time-varying all-pass filters when the input is already sample bounded
the guard diverts coefficients from their commanded trajectory and therefore changes phase and group-delay behavior for a finite interval
the stated output bound applies to Direct Form I sample output and does not establish internal-state safety for other realizations
sample-peak protection is not reconstructed true-peak or intersample-peak protection
the equal split of the second-order clipping-prevention budget is a heuristic rather than a proven optimum
evidence consists of controlled near-full-scale sinusoid tests and one music excerpt without a listening test or broad program corpus
source_updates.limited_conclusion: Use the guard only as a topology-specific candidate safety layer whose coefficient error, phase trajectory, internal states and true peak still require independent testing; it is not a general limiter or declipper.

findings: the repository has no root licence; the paper's CC-BY-4.0 notice does not establish code or bundled-audio rights
bundled SoundCam RIRs and MedleyDB mixes have no per-file rights manifest and were not accepted as project references
the save path independently peak-normalizes each input, desired, no-EQ and EQ WAV before the metrics script reloads them
independent serialization normalization invalidates absolute-gain and LUFS-difference interpretation and can change waveform metric rankings
the packaged config declares max_num_songs equal to 2 while the packaged metrics report n_files equal to 10, so they cannot be attributed to one reproducible run without reconciliation
the environment omits optional metric dependencies and the shipped table records missing MRSTFT and spectral-centroid values
the repository target builder includes an undocumented factor of one half that requires an explicit sensitivity audit
targeted searches found the official paper but no public code, deterministic implementation or test vectors
the derivation could not be checked against a runnable implementation

knowledge_cards.claim: Adaptive room equalization evidence does not establish a creative track-EQ rule.
An adaptive calibration target must be independently defined and spatially scoped before optimization.
Online transfer-function estimator confidence is part of controller safety, not merely measurement quality.
Frame, smoothing and optimizer values from one simulated room are scenario-specific rather than portable presets.
Kernel runtime without I/O, scheduling jitter and target-hardware tests is not deployment latency.
Independent per-render peak normalization destroys absolute-gain and loudness-difference evidence.
A saved config and metrics table with incompatible file counts do not describe one reproducible run.
Paper, code, dataset and bundled-audio rights require separate verification.
An all-pass clipping guard changes the commanded coefficient and phase trajectory.
A discrete sample-output bound is not an internal-state or reconstructed true-peak bound.
A Direct Form I proof cannot be transferred to arbitrary all-pass realizations without state analysis.
A sine case study and one music excerpt without listening do not prove perceptual transparency.

rule_candidates.apply_when: evaluating adaptive room or playback calibration
rule_candidates.change: keep it outside creative track processing and require an explicit listening-position scope
rule_candidates.verify: fixed-program multi-position raw A/B with independent target
rule_candidates.cancel: one position improves while other protected positions regress or the mix target is altered

rule_candidates.change: use an independently specified target and document position or zone weighting
rule_candidates.verify: compare initial-RIR-derived and external targets with optimizer fixed
rule_candidates.cancel: the controller merely preserves an arbitrary initial transfer or creates position-dependent harm

rule_candidates.apply_when: the online room estimate is low-information or non-finite
rule_candidates.change: freeze or fail closed using a preregistered estimator-confidence gate
rule_candidates.verify: dropout, low-SNR, silence and motion stress tests
rule_candidates.cancel: coefficients move during invalid or low-confidence estimates

rule_candidates.apply_when: computing gain, loudness or waveform metrics
rule_candidates.change: retain gain-preserving float outputs and forbid independent per-render peak normalization
rule_candidates.verify: in-memory versus serialized null and metric agreement
rule_candidates.cancel: serialization changes a metric or system ranking

rule_candidates.change: require config hash, input manifest, code revision and consistent file counts
rule_candidates.verify: reconstruct every result row from one manifest
rule_candidates.cancel: saved config and metric cardinality cannot be reconciled

rule_candidates.change: limit use to a verified Direct Form I path with bounded input and observed states
rule_candidates.verify: sample, reconstructed true-peak and internal-state stress tests
rule_candidates.cancel: topology differs, input bound is violated or internal state clips

rule_candidates.change: log commanded and applied coefficients plus phase and group-delay error
rule_candidates.verify: raw null, coefficient lag and blind transient checks
rule_candidates.cancel: the guard audibly smears attacks, moves the image or creates unacceptable phase-path error

rule_candidates.apply_when: deciding whether to deploy the guard
rule_candidates.change: keep it disabled until true peak, states, rapid automation, real music and target hardware pass
rule_candidates.cancel: any safety or perceptual gate fails

experiments.title: gain-preserving serialization metric audit
experiments.baseline: current independently peak-normalized saved WAV path
experiments.variant: float gain-preserving serialization of the same in-memory outputs
experiments.loudness_matching: none for raw metrics; separate BS.1770-matched copies only for blind listening
experiments.success: serialized raw metrics reproduce in-memory metrics within declared numeric tolerance and rankings remain stable
experiments.cancel: normalization or serialization changes any decision metric or ranking

experiments.title: adaptive room-EQ target-anchor A/B
experiments.baseline: target derived from the initial room impulse response
experiments.variant: independently predefined target with identical controller
experiments.cancel: benefit is position-specific, unstable or preference is loudness-driven

experiments.title: online estimator oracle-gap test
experiments.cancel: estimated path diverges, chatters or updates during invalid estimates

experiments.title: time-varying all-pass guard A/B
experiments.loudness_matching: none for safety metrics; separate BS.1770-matched blind copies
experiments.cancel: true peak or a state clips, phase error is excessive, attacks smear or image stability regresses
